title: What did you do yesterday? — the past tense
goal: Tell what has already happened using the past marker *-t*, with the two sets of endings you already know from units 10 and 11.
bekal: form the past tense of any regular verb
choose between the indefinite and definite set in the past
use *volt* and *nem volt* for states that are over

dialogs.title: Dialogue — Mit csináltál tegnap?
dialogs.intro: Monday morning in the classroom, before the lesson starts.

lines.speaker: Anna:
lines.id: Hi! What did you do yesterday?

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.id: I worked all day. And you?

lines.speaker: Anna:
lines.text: Én nem dolgoztam. Otthon maradtam és olvastam.
lines.id: I didn't work. I just stayed home and read.
lines.literal: I not I-worked-PAST. home-at I I-stayed-PAST and I-read-PAST.

lines.speaker: Anna:
lines.text: Egy magyar regényt. Nehéz volt, de tetszett.
lines.id: A Hungarian novel. It was hard, but I liked it.
lines.literal: a Hungarian novel-OBJ. hard was-PAST, but it-pleased-PAST.

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.id: What did you do in the evening?

lines.speaker: Anna:
lines.id: We had dinner at a restaurant with my friends.

lines.speaker: Anna:
lines.text: Nagyon. Halászlét rendeltünk, és sokat beszélgettünk.
lines.id: Very good. We ordered fish soup and talked a lot.
lines.literal: very. fish-soup-OBJ we-ordered-PAST, and much-OBJ we-chatted-PAST.

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: Én csak tévét néztem és korán pihentem.
lines.id: I just watched TV and went to bed early.
lines.literal: I only TV-OBJ I-watched-PAST and early-ly I-rested-PAST.

lines.speaker: Anna:
lines.text: Nem baj. Ma este együtt vacsorázunk!
lines.id: No problem. Tonight we're having dinner together!
lines.literal: no problem. today evening together we-dine!

notes: **The past marker is -t, and it comes before the person ending.** *csinál* → *csinál**t**am*, *dolgozik* → *dolgoz**t**am*, *olvas* → *olvas**t**am*. Every Hungarian past form contains this letter; if you can't find it, the sentence isn't past.

**The "I" form is the same in both sets.** *Olvastam egy könyvet* and *Olvastam a könyvet* use exactly the same form. A small, pleasant saving: in the past you only need to choose the set for five persons, not six.

**Maradtam, but olvasott.** There are two patterns: some verbs attach *-t* directly, some need a linking vowel *-ott / -ett / -ött*. The table below gives the rule, and it can be guessed from the last letter of the stem.

**Volt is the past of van — and also of nincs.** *Nehéz volt* (it was hard), *Jó volt?* (was it good?). The negative is *nem volt*, not *nincs volt*: *nincs* only lives in the present, and once the story shifts into the past, it disappears completely.

**Note that volt must appear even though it's absent in the present.** Compare *Nehéz* (hard — present, no verb) with *Nehéz volt* (it was hard — past). The empty box from unit 1 is empty only in the present; in the past it is filled.

**Tetszett** uses a pattern that flips the subject: the thing that pleases is the book, not Anna. Literally "it pleased". English words it the usual way ("I liked"), so this form must be memorized whole: *Tetszett a film* = "I liked the film".

grammars.title: The -t marker: direct or with a linking vowel
body: The last letter of the stem decides.
after: **That linking vowel appears only in the *ő* form.** Compare *olvas**ott*** (he/she read) but *olvas**t**am*, *olvas**t**ál*, *olvas**t**unk*. Once a person ending is there, the linking vowel is no longer needed.

**A few rebels, all of them common:** two-syllable verbs ending in *-ad / -ed* take *-t* directly — *marad* → *maradt*, *szalad* → *szaladt* — while *hall*, on the contrary, takes the linking vowel: *hallott*. There are few of them; memorize them as you meet them.
Irregular verbs — *van, megy, jön, eszik, iszik, tesz, vesz* — have their own past forms, and that is the content of unit 19.

grammars.title: Person endings in the past
body: Two sets, just like in the present. Note the first row: the forms are identical.
after: For front-vowel verbs, the vowel of the ending adjusts: *kér* → *kértem, kértél, kért, kértünk, kértetek, kértek* (indefinite) and *kértem, kérted, kérte, kértük, kértétek, kérték* (definite).

**The rule for choosing the set is exactly the same as in unit 11.** An object with *a/az*, a proper name, a demonstrative, a possessive ending, *őt/őket* → definite. Everything else is indefinite. There's no new rule to memorize here — only the new forms.

grammars.title: Volt — the past of van
body: One verb, but the one you'll use most in the past.
after: The negatives are *nem voltam*, *nem volt*, and so on. The word *nincs* has no past form at all: "there wasn't" in the past is always *nem volt*.

*Volt* is also used to express experience: *Voltál már Szegeden?* = "Have you been to Szeged?". The word *már* (already) turns it into a question about experience, and the answer is *Igen, voltam* or *Nem, még nem*.

blocks.text: Notice *egy órája* and *két napja*: they use a possessive ending, literally "its one hour", "its two days". Compare *egy óra múlva* (in an hour) from unit 9 — one looks backward, the other faces forward.

blocks.title: The most useful writing exercise at this level
items: Write five sentences about your day yesterday, using only regular verbs you already know. Five sentences, not five paragraphs.
Then turn them all into a story about a friend — every verb in the *ő* form. Then turn them into a story about the two of you — all *mi*.
Those three rounds lock in the whole past-tense table without you ever having to stare at it.
